# 1 INTRODUCTION

Text-conditioned 3D human–object interaction (HOI) generation aims to synthesize human motion and object dynamics from a language description and has attracted increasing attention (Li et al., 2024; Cha et al., 2024; Peng et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2026b). In particular, generating one interaction counterpart, as demonstrated by OMOMO (Li et al., 2023) and DAViD (Kim et al., 2025), has shown promising results. However, joint generation of plausible human and object motions remains challenging and relatively underexplored. Since individual plausibility does not ensure interaction coherence, simply combining the generated object and human motion trajectories may exhibit spatial misalignment or frequent interpenetration, which we define as a lack of coordination.

Extensive experiments demonstrate that [NAME C07] consistently outperforms prior methods in overall generation quality and human-object coordination. These advantages remain evident in long-horizon generation, where [NAME C07] preserves coherent interactions as the requested duration extends beyond the fixed training window. Our contributions are as follows:

- We propose [NAME C07], a unified latent framework for text-conditioned HOI generation at any requested duration. By explicitly modeling continuous human-object geometry, [NAME C07] learns coordinated dynamics directly from data without contact-specific regularization or heuristic interaction designs.
- We introduce a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) autoencoder that jointly encodes human, object, and relation modalities via modality-specific transformations and relation-aware decoding.
- We design a blockwise Flow Forcing scheme to align finite-window training with progressive rollout, enabling stable HOI generation beyond the training horizon.

We use ChatGPT and OpenAI Codex to assist with the refinement of some internal module designs, parts of the implementation, literature search and summarization, and language polishing. The core research idea, overall architecture, experimental design and evaluation protocols, result interpretation, dataset processing, qualitative analysis, and mathematical formulation are developed and conducted by the authors without generative AI assistance. All AI-assisted design suggestions, code, and literature references are independently reviewed and verified by the authors, who take full responsibility for the final content of the paper and associated artifacts.

# A SUPPLEMENTARY METHOD DETAILS

## A.1 STRUCTURED AUTOENCODER

**Token construction.** Considering that the marker-level human and relation fields are substantially denser than the rigid-object state, we first reduce them to comparable token sets without removing their spatial organization. At each frame, eight learned body-region queries aggregate the 77 surface markers, while separate root and foot tokens retain global translation and support information. This construction yields 11 human tokens per frame. Given the rigid structure of the object, we use one dynamic pose token per frame and four static geometry tokens obtained from its Basis Point Set (BPS) descriptor (Prokudin et al., 2019). To preserve the correspondence between motion and relation features, eight relation queries aggregate marker-level relations and two additional tokens retain the object–ground and root–object relations, yielding 10 relation tokens per frame. ## Abstract

The success of deep generative models in generating high-quality and diverse samples is often attributed to particular architectures and large training datasets. In this paper, we investigate the impact of these factors on the quality and diversity of samples generated by flow-matching models. Surprisingly, in our experiments on CelebA-HQ dataset, flow matching remains stable even when pruning 50% of the dataset. That is, the quality and diversity of generated samples are preserved. Moreover, pruning impacts the latent representation only slightly, that is, samples generated by models trained on the full and pruned dataset map to visually similar outputs for a given seed. We observe similar stability when changing the architecture or training configuration, such that the latent representati

not shown for FM models, nor was it shown how this invariance can be exploited to train diffusion models on less data. Furthermore, in diffusion models, the objective is related to entropic-transport optimization (Schrödinger bridge) [6], which is stable to data perturbations [11]. By contrast, the flow-matching objective fits a velocity field $u(x, t)$, whose ODE transports noisy latents towards a clean manifold. While diffusion's stability is theoretically grounded, the behavior of FM models under data and architectural perturbations remains largely underexplored.

We empirically analyze the behavior of FM models trained on subsets of data and with different architectures.

We summarize our contributions as follows:

- We show that FM models are remarkably stable. The generated images are visually similar under a wide variety of perturbations, including training on disjoint subsets of the dataset, swapping of the entire dataset, as well as model architecture shrinkage. Each perturbation affects the generated data semantically only minimally.
- Inspired by previous work in discriminative models, we introduce three informed data pruning methods to FM models and study their influence qualitatively and quantitatively.
- Our proposed cluster-based resampling method th

The nearest samples form a representative subset retaining the core characteristics of the distribution, while the furthest samples cover more difficult and scarce samples. We refer to these variants as  \( Clust_{p/b}^{1/-1} \) , indicating nearest/furthest and proportional/balanced. In our experiments, we choose k = 24 based on analysis of the clusters' inertia.

## 1 Introduction

Diffusion models [[29](#bib.bib11), [30](#bib.bib10)] have driven tremendous advances in generative modeling over the past few years [[27](#bib.bib27), [13](#bib.bib13), [4](#bib.bib14), [20](#bib.bib9)]. Flow-matching (FM) methods, an alternative to diffusion models [[14](#bib.bib12)], promise several advantages in efficiency and simplicity while achieving competitive performance [[18](#bib.bib15), [19](#bib.bib16), [31](#bib.bib17), [1](#bib.bib8), [20](#bib.bib9)]. Yet, training these models remains demanding both in compute and data, therefore, tailoring a dataset to desired generative properties has the potential to significantly reduce the computational cost. In this paper, we study the stability of FM under data perturbation, and develop informed approaches to data pruning. Using standard metrics, we probe stability and find a surprising result: even under strong perturbation of data and model architecture, trajectories initialized with the same random noise evolve to visually similar samples.

# The Amazing Stability of Flow Matching

###### Abstract

The success of deep generative models in generating high-quality and diverse samples is often attributed to particular architectures and large training datasets. In this paper, we investigate the impact of these factors on the quality and diversity of samples generated by *flow-matching* models. Surprisingly, in our experiments on CelebA-HQ dataset, flow matching remains stable even when pruning 50% of the dataset. That is, the quality and diversity of generated samples are preserved. Moreover, pruning impacts the latent representation only slightly, that is, samples generated by models trained on the full and pruned dataset map to visually similar outputs for a given seed. We observe similar stability when changing the architecture or training configuration, such that the latent representation is maintained under these changes as well.
Our results quantify just how strong this stability can be in practice, and help explain the reliability of flow-matching models under various perturbations.

# 1 INTRODUCTION

Text-conditioned 3D human–object interaction (HOI) generation aims to synthesize human motion and object dynamics from a language description and has attracted increasing attention (Li et al., 2024; Cha et al., 2024; Peng et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2026b). In particular, generating one interaction counterpart, as demonstrated by OMOMO (Li et al., 2023) and DAViD (Kim et al., 2025), has shown promising results. However, joint generation of plausible human and object motions remains challenging and relatively underexplored. Since individual plausibility does not ensure interaction coherence, simply combining the generated object and human motion trajectories may exhibit spatial misalignment or frequent interpenetration, which we define as a lack of coordination.

Our contributions are as follows:

- We propose [NAME C07], a unified latent framework for text-conditioned HOI generation at any requested duration. By explicitly modeling continuous human-object geometry, [NAME C07] learns coordinated dynamics directly from data without contact-specific regularization or heuristic interaction designs.
- We introduce a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) autoencoder that jointly encodes human, object, and relation modalities via modality-specific transformations and relation-aware decoding.
- We design a blockwise Flow Forcing scheme to align finite-window training with progressive rollout, enabling stable HOI generation beyond the training horizon.

## A.1 STRUCTURED AUTOENCODER

**Token construction.** Considering that the marker-level human and relation fields are substantially denser than the rigid-object state, we first reduce them to comparable token sets without removing their spatial organization. At each frame, eight learned body-region queries aggregate the 77 surface markers, while separate root and foot tokens retain global translation and support information. This construction yields 11 human tokens per frame. Given the rigid structure of the object, we use one dynamic pose token per frame and four static geometry tokens obtained from its Basis Point Set (BPS) descriptor (Prokudin et al., 2019). To preserve the correspondence between motion and relation features, eight relation queries aggregate marker-level relations and two additional tokens retain the object–ground and root–object relations, yielding 10 relation tokens per frame.
